groups.title: Tablet (E66700ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to supply vitamin D, vitamin E, vitamin B1, vitamin B2, vitamin B6 and vitamin C during physical fatigue, pregnancy and breast-feeding, when strength is reduced during or after illness, during the growing years and in old age; for poor development of the bones and teeth and the prevention of rickets; for beriberi and eye fatigue; to relieve neuralgia, muscle pain and joint pain (low back pain, stiff shoulders and the like); to relieve angular cheilitis, cheilitis, stomatitis, glossitis, eczema and dermatitis; and to supply zinc.
groups.usage: Adults and people aged 8 years and over: take 1 tablet at a time, once a day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have high blood calcium, sarcoidosis, kidney disease, kidney stones or severe kidney failure; if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption; or if the user is a baby under 12 months of age.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, or are breast-feeding; if the user is a premature baby or a young child; if you have hyperoxaluria; if you have a gastrointestinal disease such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis or regional enteritis; if you have impaired cardiac or circulatory function, kidney impairment or low blood protein; or if you have gout, or have or have had kidney stones.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. This medicine may interfere with the detection of glucose in various urine tests and may turn the urine yellow, which can affect laboratory test results.

Do not take this medicine together with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations, antacids or levodopa. Consult a doctor or a pharmacist before taking it with oral contraceptives that contain oestrogen. Take care when it is given together with anti-aldosterone medicines or triamterene, because this may cause high blood potassium. Avoid tannin-containing teas such as green tea and black tea while taking this medicine and just before or after taking it.

If nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, constipation, rash, redness of the skin, loose stools, red spots, cardiac arrest, reduced central nervous system function, dermatitis, a bad smell in the sweat or breath, hair loss, restlessness, gastrointestinal disturbance, digestive problems, upper abdominal pain, low blood pressure or fluid on the lungs appears; if a period comes earlier than expected, becomes gradually heavier or the bleeding lasts a long time; or if there is no improvement in symptoms after about 1 month of use, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Supply of vitamins D, E, B1, B2, B6 and C and of zinc; bone and tooth development; beriberi; eye fatigue; neuralgia and muscle/joint pain; cheilitis, stomatitis, glossitis, eczema, dermatitis
summaryTable.Choosing a product: Products with the same generic-name code (E66700ATB) share the same ingredient, strength and dosage form. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the brand name.
summaryTable.Ask the pharmacist: Ask the pharmacist in the store first if any of the cautions above apply to you.

groups.title: Syrup (172838ASY)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for rheumatoid arthritis, juvenile rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis (degenerative joint disease), fever and pain caused by a cold, low back pain, period pain, pain after surgery, ankylosing spondylitis, headache, toothache, muscle pain, neuralgia, acute gout, psoriatic arthritis, soft-tissue injury (sprain, contusion) and non-articular rheumatic disease (tendinitis, tenosynovitis, bursitis).
groups.usage: For rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, soft-tissue injury, non-articular rheumatic disease, acute gout and psoriatic arthritis, adults take 200 to 600 mg at a time, 3 to 4 times a day; up to a maximum of 3200 mg a day may be taken. For juvenile rheumatoid arthritis, take 30 to 40 mg per kg of body weight a day, divided into 3 to 4 doses. For mild to moderate pain or a cold, adults take 200 to 400 mg at a time, 3 to 4 times a day. Ages 11 to 14 years: take 200 to 250 mg (5 to 6.5 mL) at a time. Ages 7 to 10 years: 150 to 200 mg (4 to 5 mL) at a time. Ages 3 to 6 years: 100 to 150 mg (2.5 to 4 mL) at a time. Ages 1 to 2 years: 50 to 100 mg (1.5 to 2.5 mL) at a time. Take the dose 3 to 4 times a day. In children weighing less than 30 kg the daily dose must not exceed 500 mg (12.5 mL), and it is better to avoid taking it on an empty stomach. Do not take more than the recommended dose.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day, consult a doctor or a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause bleeding in the digestive tract.

Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious and possibly fatal cardiovascular thrombotic events, myocardial infarction and stroke, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulceration and perforation may occur.

Patients with uncontrolled high blood pressure, congestive heart failure, established ischaemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease or cerebrovascular disease should avoid high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg a day). Patients with cardiovascular risk factors (high blood pressure, high blood lipids, diabetes, smoking and the like) should consult a doctor or a pharmacist before taking this medicine if high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg a day) is needed.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have gastrointestinal ulcer or gastrointestinal bleeding or have had them in the past; if you have a severe blood disorder, severe liver impairment, severe kidney impairment, severe heart failure or severe high blood pressure; if you have bronchial asthma or have had it in the past; if you have had hypersensitivity such as asthma, hives or an allergic reaction to aspirin or other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics (including COX-2 inhibitors); if you have pain before or after coronary artery bypass grafting; or if you are in the last three months of pregnancy or are breast-feeding.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you have or have had a blood disorder; if you have a tendency to bleed; if you have or have had liver cirrhosis or liver impairment, or kidney impairment; if you have heart failure or heart disease, high blood pressure, systemic lupus erythematosus or mixed connective tissue disease, ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease; if the user is an older person or a child; if you are pregnant or breast-feeding; or if you have a disorder of fat metabolism such as hyperlipoproteinaemia, diabetic hyperlipidaemia or pancreatitis.

Do not take this medicine together with other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics, low-dose aspirin or high-dose methotrexate. Consult a doctor or a pharmacist before using it with ACE inhibitors, lithium, furosemide and thiazide diuretics, coumarin anticoagulants (warfarin and the like), selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors or intravenous lipid preparations.

If signs of shock (difficulty breathing, a fall in blood pressure and the like); blood disorders such as reduced haematocrit, reduced haemoglobin, anaemia, aplastic anaemia, haemolytic anaemia, agranulocytosis, granulocytopenia, low white blood cell count, low platelet count, reduced platelet function or raised eosinophils; peptic ulcer, gastrointestinal ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, perforation, ulcerative colitis, blood in the stools, gastritis, pancreatitis, vomiting of blood, Crohn's disease, loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, indigestion, diarrhoea, stomach (upper abdominal) discomfort, upper abdominal pain, thirst, inflammation of the mouth, abdominal bloating, mouth ulcers, constipation or black stools; Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome) of unknown frequency, angioneurotic oedema, bullous dermatitis, erythema multiforme, maculopapular rash, reddening of the skin, blisters, rash, exfoliative dermatitis or acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis; hepatitis, jaundice, abnormal liver function such as raised GOT, GPT or ALP, or liver impairment; hypersensitivity or anaphylactic reaction, asthma attack, hives, eczema, purple spots, rash, itching, asthma, bronchial constriction, difficulty breathing or wheezing; visual disturbance such as blind spots, deafness, ringing in the ears, taste disturbance, light-headedness, drowsiness, dizziness, depression, headache, a cerebrovascular event or nervousness; aseptic meningitis or meningitis (severe headache, nausea, vomiting, insomnia, a stiff neck, fever or impaired consciousness and the like); a fall or rise in blood pressure, palpitations, heart failure, myocardial infarction or angina; acute kidney failure, reduced urine output, blood in the urine, protein in the urine, raised BUN or blood creatinine, high blood potassium, interstitial nephritis, nephrotic syndrome, renal papillary necrosis, reduced urine volume, generalised swelling with shortness of breath and lassitude, swelling around the eyes, facial swelling, lassitude, fever, nosebleed, swelling or swelling of the limbs appears, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

groups.title: Soft capsule (395900ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for cough and phlegm.
groups.usage: Adults and people aged 15 years and over: take 1 capsule at a time, 3 times a day, after meals.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you are pregnant or may be pregnant; if the user is a baby under 3 months of age or a child under 2 years of age; or if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, antiparkinsonian medicine and the like) or stopped taking one within the past 2 weeks.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you have an allergic constitution or have had an allergic reaction to a medicine (for example fever, rash, joint pain or itching); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, glaucoma (for example eye pain or blurred vision) or difficulty passing urine; if the user is an older person, is debilitated or has a high fever; if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, or are breast-feeding; or if you have a cough associated with smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis or emphysema, a cough with excessive phlegm, a cough that lasts or returns for more than 1 week, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever, rash or persistent headache.

If there is no improvement after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist. For babies and young children aged 7 years and under, give the syrup form instead. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Drowsiness may occur after taking this medicine, so take care when driving or operating machinery.

Do not take this medicine together with other antitussives and expectorants, cold medicines, oral medicines containing an antihistamine (oral medicines for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicines, allergy medicines) or sedatives. Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine.

If rash, redness (congested and reddened skin), itching, nausea or vomiting, loss of appetite, dizziness, difficulty passing urine, thirst (persistent or severe), anxiety, tremor or insomnia appears, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

groups.title: Oral liquid (D61400ALQ)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to relieve the various symptoms of a cold (sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills (feeling cold and shivery), fever, headache, joint pain and muscle pain).
groups.usage: Adults and people aged 15 years and over: take 1 sachet at a time, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals. If needed, a dose may be taken at bedtime; leave an interval of 4 hours between doses.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day, consult a doctor or a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal — acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis — have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of a hypersensitivity reaction appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take this medicine together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, if you have had asthma after taking another antipyretic analgesic or cold medicine, or if the user is a child under 2 years of age.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if the user is an infant or a child under 15 years of age who has, or is suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if you have an allergic constitution or have had an allergic reaction to a medicine (for example fever, rash, joint pain, asthma or itching); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, swelling or gastric or duodenal ulcer; if the user is an older person, is debilitated or has a high fever; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or have ulcer or bleeding problems; if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, or are breast-feeding; or if you have a cough associated with smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis or emphysema, a cough with excessive phlegm, a cough that lasts or returns for more than 1 week, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever, rash or persistent headache.

If there is no improvement after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

Do not take this medicine together with oral medicines that contain an expectorant (phlegm medicine), another cold medicine, an antipyretic analgesic, a sedative or an antihistamine (oral medicines for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicines, allergy medicines). Do not take this medicine if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, antiparkinsonian medicine and the like) or stopped taking one within the past 2 weeks. Consult a doctor or a pharmacist before taking it with barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, alcohol, potassium-containing preparations, liquorice-containing preparations, preparations containing glycyrrhizic acid or its salts, loop diuretics (furosemide, etacrynic acid), thiazide diuretics (trichlormethiazide), medicines for diabetes, gout or arthritis, anticoagulants or steroids. Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine.

If rash, redness (congested and reddened skin), itching, nausea or vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, swelling, dizziness, or — rarely — signs of shock (hives, swelling and chest tightness immediately after taking the medicine, together with a pale face, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (severe symptoms such as high fever with reddening of the skin and burn-like blistering on the skin of the whole body or on the lining of the mouth or eyes), asthma, general lassitude, jaundice, interstitial pneumonia (dry cough, fever and the like), reduced urine output with swelling of the face and limbs, heavy eyelids, stiff hands, a rise in blood pressure or headache, or myopathy (weakness, cramp of the arms or legs, paralysis) appears, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

groups.title: Eye drops (D60100COS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for washing the eyes, for eye discomfort after swimming, and when dust or sweat has got into the eyes.
groups.usage: Wash the eye using 5 mL at a time, 3 to 6 times a day.
groups.caution:
Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you have severe eye pain, if you have had hypersensitivity to an eye medicine, or if you have dry eye syndrome.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is used for a child, use it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian. Use this medicine only for washing the eyes. Do not use it as a wetting solution for contact lenses or while contact lenses are being worn. To prevent contamination, do not share the eye cup with others. Do not use it on an injured eye.

If redness of the eye, itching, swelling, or skin rash, redness or itching appears, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

groups.usage: Adults and children aged 12 years and over: take 2 capsules (650 mg) at a time, 3 to 4 times a day (every 4 to 6 hours), when needed. Do not take more than a maximum of 12 capsules (4000 mg) a day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, peptic ulcer, a severe blood disorder, severe liver impairment, severe kidney impairment or severely reduced heart function; if you have aspirin-induced asthma (asthma attacks triggered by non-steroidal anti-inflammatory medicines) or have had it in the past; if you have taken barbiturates or tricyclic antidepressants; or if you have drunk alcohol.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you have liver impairment, kidney impairment, peptic ulcer, a blood disorder, a tendency to bleed or abnormal heart function; if you have had a hypersensitivity reaction; if you have bronchial asthma; if the user is an older person; or if you are pregnant or breast-feeding.

If pain or fever lasts or gets worse, or if a new symptom appears, consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine together with other products containing acetaminophen, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol. Consult a doctor or a pharmacist before taking it with warfarin, lithium, thiazide diuretics or other anti-inflammatory analgesics.

If signs of shock (difficulty breathing, flushing of the whole body, angioedema, hives, an asthma attack and the like), low platelet count, granulocytopenia, haemolytic anaemia, methaemoglobinaemia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time), cyanosis, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, skin rash, Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), raised AST, raised ALT, itchy rash or fixed drug eruption appears, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for drowsiness and for recovery from tiredness.
groups.usage: Adults and children aged 15 years and over: take 2 tablets at a time, 1 to 2 times a day, leaving an interval of at least 6 hours.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have symptoms of excess stomach acid, heart disease or gastric ulcer, or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you are under a doctor's care, or if you are pregnant or may be pregnant or are breast-feeding. People under 15 years of age must not take this medicine.

Do not take this medicine together with other anti-drowsiness medicines or with caffeine-containing drinks (coffee, tea and the like).

If rash, loss of appetite, nausea or vomiting, tremor, light-headedness, anxiety, insomnia, headache or palpitations appears, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

groups.title: Eye gel (124204COO)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to relieve the symptoms of dry eyes.
groups.usage: Adults: depending on how severe the symptoms are, instil 1 drop into the conjunctival sac at a time, 1 to 4 times a day; for use at bedtime, instil it about 30 minutes beforehand. Treatment of dry keratoconjunctivitis generally needs long-term or continuous treatment, so you should consult an eye specialist.
groups.caution:
Do not use this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it.

Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you have severe eye pain; if you have had an allergic reaction to an eye medicine (redness of the eye, itching, swelling, reddening of the skin and the like); if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, or are breast-feeding; or if the user is a child.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Use this medicine only in the eye. Remove contact lenses before use and put them back in 30 minutes after instilling this medicine. If you are using other eye preparations at the same time, leave an interval of at least 15 minutes and always use this medicine last. Blurred vision may occur after use, so take care when driving or operating machinery. Close the cap after use. Instil small drops to keep the eyelids from sticking together. To prevent contamination, avoid sharing the product with others where possible.

If mild irritation, or — rarely — punctate keratitis, ulcerative keratitis, fever, sticking of the eyelashes, redness of the eye, giant papillary conjunctivitis of the eyelid, corneal spots, episcleritis, blurred vision, itching or discomfort appears, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery. If there is no improvement after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine together with oral medicines that contain an antitussive or expectorant, another cold medicine, an antipyretic analgesic, a sedative or an antihistamine (oral medicines for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicines, allergy medicines). Consult a doctor or a pharmacist before taking it with barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, alcohol, medicines for diabetes, gout or arthritis, anticoagulants or steroids. Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine.

If rash, redness, itching, nausea or vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, swelling, difficulty passing urine, thirst (persistent or severe), dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, or — rarely — signs of shock (hives, swelling and chest tightness immediately after taking the medicine, together with a pale face, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (severe symptoms such as high fever with rash, redness and burn-like blistering), acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis (a serious skin reaction with fever, redness of the skin and many small pustules), asthma, general lassitude, jaundice or interstitial pneumonia (cough, shortness of breath, difficulty breathing, fever) appears, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

If symptoms of posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome or reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome (sudden severe headache, thunderclap headache, nausea, vomiting, confusion, seizure, visual disturbance and the like) appear, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

For fungal nail infection of the finger and toe nails, cut the nails short and spread a thin layer 1 time a day (at bedtime if possible), or 2 times a day (morning and evening) if needed. Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you are pregnant or may be pregnant or are breast-feeding, or if the user is a child.

Do not use an occlusive dressing or wrapping unless a doctor tells you to. If you have candidiasis, do not use acidic soap.

Consult a doctor or a pharmacist before using it together with other medicines applied to the skin.

If irritation or sensitivity appears, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist. Rarely, a burning feeling, a stinging sensation, dryness, redness of the skin, itching or local irritation may occur.

groups.title: Tablet (199402ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis (degenerative joint disease), ankylosing spondylitis, tendinitis, acute gout, period pain, bursitis, skeletal muscle disorders (sprains, bruises, wounds, low back pain), pain after surgery, migraine and pain after tooth extraction.
groups.usage: For rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis and ankylosing spondylitis, adults take 1 to 2 tablets (250 to 500 mg) at a time, 2 times a day (every 12 hours). For acute gout, adults take 3 tablets (750 mg) as the first dose, then 1 tablet (250 mg) every 8 hours until the attack has gone. For skeletal muscle disorders, pain after surgery, pain after tooth extraction, period pain, tendinitis and bursitis, adults take 2 tablets (500 mg) as the first dose, then 1 tablet (250 mg) every 6 to 8 hours; the total daily dose must not exceed 5 tablets (1250 mg). For migraine, adults take 3 tablets (750 mg) as the first dose and, if needed, a further 1 to 2 tablets (250 to 500 mg) a day given 30 minutes after the first dose; the total daily dose must not exceed 5 tablets (1250 mg).
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day, consult a doctor or a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause bleeding in the digestive tract.

Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious and possibly fatal cardiovascular thrombotic events, myocardial infarction and stroke, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulceration and perforation may occur.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or to non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics such as aspirin; if you have had asthma, rhinitis, nasal polyps, hives or an allergic reaction to other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics (including COX-2 inhibitors); if you have peptic ulcer, a severe blood disorder, severe liver impairment, severe heart failure, severe kidney impairment or severe high blood pressure; if you are pregnant or breast-feeding; if the user is a baby aged 2 years or under; or for the treatment of pain occurring before or after coronary artery bypass grafting.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you are pregnant or may be pregnant; if the user is a child or an older person; if you have had a peptic ulcer; if you have or have had a blood disorder; if you have a tendency to bleed; if you have or have had liver impairment; if you have or have had kidney impairment or reduced blood flow to the kidneys; or if you have impaired heart function, high blood pressure, systemic lupus erythematosus or mixed connective tissue disease.

Do not take this medicine together with other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics, aspirin or high-dose methotrexate. Consult a doctor or a pharmacist before taking it with hydantoin antiepileptics, sulfonamides, sulfonylurea blood-sugar-lowering medicines, propranolol and other beta-blockers, ACE inhibitors (captopril and the like), loop diuretics and thiazide diuretics, probenecid, lithium, low-dose methotrexate, coumarin anticoagulants (warfarin and the like), zidovudine or new-quinolone antibiotics (enoxacin and the like).

If signs of shock (difficulty breathing, a fall in blood pressure, a slow heartbeat, cold sweat, swelling and the like) or PIE syndrome (pulmonary infiltration with eosinophilia: fever, wheezing, cough and phlegm) — which occur rarely — or hives, or — occasionally — rash, itching or other hypersensitivity symptoms appear; or — rarely — vomiting of blood, bleeding in the digestive tract, peptic ulcer, perforation, stomach discomfort, stomach pain, abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, indigestion, heartburn, diarrhoea, constipation, inflammation of the mouth, abdominal bloating, black stools or thirst; or — rarely — blood disorders such as agranulocytosis, raised eosinophils, low white blood cell count, low platelet count, aplastic anaemia, haemolytic anaemia or reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time); raised GOT and GPT, jaundice, hepatitis; kidney impairment, glomerulonephritis, blood in the urine, high blood potassium, interstitial nephritis, nephrotic syndrome, renal papillary necrosis, protein in the urine or kidney failure; or — rarely — aseptic meningitis (severe headache, nausea, vomiting, insomnia, a stiff neck, fever or impaired consciousness and the like); or — occasionally — drowsiness or impaired thinking, or — rarely — dizziness, headache, numb hands and feet, reduced sex drive, tiredness, depression, abnormal dreams, loss of concentration, disorientation, insomnia, muscle pain or muscle weakness; or — occasionally — eczema, sweating or purple spots, or — rarely — photosensitivity, hair loss, redness (congested and reddened skin), necrolysis, erythema multiforme, exfoliative dermatitis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), hives, epidermolysis bullosa, toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms or fixed drug eruption; or ringing in the ears, hearing disturbance, visual disturbance, swelling or difficulty breathing; or — rarely — palpitations, muscle weakness, congestive heart failure, eosinophilic pneumonia, an anaphylactoid reaction, menstrual disturbance, chills with fever, vasculitis, high blood sugar or low blood sugar appears, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.
